hypothesis: To empirically determine whether transformer-based sequence models (PatchTST-lite and Informer) outperform ARIMA models in forecasting daily volatility of equity index returns when transaction costs are explicitly incorporated into the performance metric using a Sharpe ratio adjusted for turnover and proportional transaction costs.
author: coder-agent
baseline: Performance of ARIMA models on the same dataset and task, serving as the standard against which transformer models are compared.
success_criteria: If the transformer models (PatchTST-lite and Informer) achieve significantly higher adjusted Sharpe ratios and/or lower MSE in volatility forecasts compared to ARIMA models, the hypothesis is supported. Conversely, if ARIMA models perform better or similarly, the hypothesis is refuted.
notes: Mixed results between transformer and ARIMA models in terms of adjusted Sharpe ratio.
